trickyParts: WORKSPACE TRAP (from plan concerns[0]) held: the working copy `@` carries a tracked 0-byte .omp/config.yml. Both commits were made with path-scoped `jj split -m '<msg>' <path>`, so .omp/config.yml stays in `@` as the remainder and never entered the pushed chain. Verified after each split with `jj status` (only `A .omp/config.yml`) and `jj diff --from main@origin --to @- --summary`.

BOOKMARK TRAP (from plan concerns[1]) held, with one wrinkle: after every `jj split`, jj moves bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-104 onto the remainder commit `@`. Re-pointing it with `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-104 -r @-` is a backwards move (`@-` is the parent of `@`), which jj refuses: `Error: Refusing to move bookmark backwards or sideways`. Every phase must use `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-104 -r @- --allow-backwards` before `jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-104`. Safe because the target is always the newest real commit on the chain; only the .omp remainder is excluded.
TOOLING TRAP (from plan concerns[7]) held: byte checks used /usr/bin/cmp, never the bash `cmp` shim.

Your handoff commit must be path-scoped: `jj split -m 'test: record handoff' .legion/test.json`, then `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-104 -r @- --allow-backwards`, then `jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-104`. Never `jj new` from `@` or `jj describe @`.
